claims.text: A machine-learning-augmented adaptive enhanced-sampling scheme can compute solid and liquid free-energy landscapes near melting.
The proposed scheme can retain vibrational-entropy, anharmonic, and electron–vibration-coupling contributions.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by 10–100 times relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
Key results from the proposed method will deviate by no more than approximately 5% from explicit ab initio MD and TOR-TILD results.
ML potentials can replace most expensive ab initio force evaluations within the sampling workflow.
Periodic ab initio recalibration will ensure retention of all relevant free-energy contributions.
The method is intended to treat both solid and fluid phases from approximately 0.8 times the melting temperature up to the melting temperature.
Prior validation in elemental and binary systems can be extended to multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Polymorphism is a relevant structural phenomenon in high-entropy alloys.
Embedding an ML potential in umbrella sampling or metadynamics will correctly capture stacking, polymorphism, and anharmonic effects.
A judiciously selected ab initio training set will allow rapid navigation of complex solid and liquid phase spaces.
Periodic ab initio corrections will keep errors in vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling low.
Accurate free energies for both phases will enable accurate derived fusion properties.
Direct free-energy methods are computationally prohibitive for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics free-energy evaluation and TOR-TILD have been validated on elemental and binary systems.
The method is expected to work from elemental systems through multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting.
Systems with anharmonicity or electron–vibration coupling outside the training set may require further refinement.
ML-potential transferability across compositions and phases is uncertain, especially for subtle free-energy contributions in high-entropy systems.
A deviation greater than approximately 5% in phase free energies or melting temperature relative to the reference workflows will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as an equilibrium solid or liquid, while the method is applied to both phases down to approximately 0.8Tm. At temperatures substantially below Tm, the liquid would ordinarily be metastable rather than the equilibrium phase unless additional pressure or metastability conditions are specified.
